spin-the-wheel.formula:
Each of the n options owns a slice of 360° ÷ n, starting at the top and going clockwise.
Winner: index = floor(random() x n) — every option has exactly a 1/n chance.
Animation: 5 to 7 full turns plus the exact offset that parks the middle of the winner's slice under the pointer at the top.
howTo: Type each option and press Add (or hit Enter). Add 2 to 12 options.
Remove any option with the x on its chip — the wheel redraws itself.
Press Spin the Wheel and watch it whirl 5 to 7 full turns with a smooth slow-down.
The pointer lands on the winner, whose chip lights up and whose win count grows by one.
Press Reset Wins anytime to zero the counts without removing your options.
keyFacts: The Decision Wheel picks one option at random from 2 to 12 choices you type in.
Every option owns an equal slice of the wheel: 360° divided by the number of options.
The winner is drawn first with a random number; the animation then aims that slice at the pointer.
Each spin runs 5 to 7 full turns with an ease-out slow-down over about 4 seconds.
A win tally tracks how many times each option has won.
The pointer sits at the top of the wheel — the slice under it when the wheel stops is the winner.

spin-the-wheel.workedExample:
8 options → each slice is 45°.
1. random() returns 0.68 → index = floor(0.68 × 8) = 5 → the 6th option.
2. Middle of slice 5 = 5 × 45° + 22.5° = 247.5° from the top. The wheel must rotate (360 − 247.5) = 112.5° (mod 360) to park it under the pointer.
3. Current rotation 0°, 6 full spins → final = 0 + 6 × 360 + 112.5 = 2272.5°. Check: (360 − 112.5) mod 360 = 247.5° → index = floor(247.5 ÷ 45) = 5. The pointer lands on option 6.
